scope: Reviewed decompositions of mixed normative paragraphs. Other paragraphs still require clause-level review; sentence splitting alone is not proof of independent obligations or coverage.

obligations.requirement: A type-cast path segment is a qualified name resolving to a type in scope; simple identifiers are member names.
A path cast evaluates to null for an incompatible preceding type or instance.
obligations.policy: The resolver binds qualified casts without requiring every runtime instance to match. Runtime instance testing and null evaluation belong to the consumer.

obligations.requirement: Term casts use qualified in-scope term names and optional simple-identifier qualifiers; implicit media terms apply to media entities and stream properties.
A term cast evaluates to null when the preceding instance lacks the term application with the specified qualifier.
obligations.policy: Static resolution retains the term and qualifier without requiring an application on every runtime instance. Value evaluation belongs to the consumer.

obligations.requirement: Concat takes at least two scalar primitive or enumeration arguments and returns Edm.String; primitive type definitions retain their underlying type compatibility.
Executing concat converts argument results to their prescribed literal representations and concatenates them.
obligations.policy: The static validator checks argument and result types without evaluating expressions. Runtime primitive/enum literal conversion and concatenation belong to the caller's expression evaluator.

obligations.requirement: A URL reference contains one scalar string expression; its literal may be relative or absolute.
Relative URL references retain their document/base-URI meaning across serialization.
obligations.policy: Serialization with source_uri preserves literal URL references using document and reference-local XML Base, including caller-supplied result types during checked output. Dynamic operands are preserved without rebasing, but rebasing rejects them before emitting bytes because their eventual relative URLs cannot be determined statically. Dynamic relocation remains unsupported.

obligations.requirement: When the caller provides the URL result type, its type and multiplicity must match the surrounding expression; unavailable result types remain explicit diagnostics.
Executing a URL reference returns the GET response body.
obligations.policy: The validator does not issue HTTP requests or execute expressions. Runtime retrieval and checking actual response values belong to the caller.

obligations.requirement: The URI-template function takes a string template followed by labeled parameter expressions.
A complex record inherits its expected type from context or explicitly names a compatible structured type; primitive, unresolved and unrelated types are invalid.
Single-valued nonnullable navigation members require a value in a record; nullable and collection-valued navigation members may be omitted.
A record supplies single-valued nonnullable structural properties without defaults; nullable/defaulted properties may be omitted.
Explicitly typed complex record collection items must be assignable to the collection element type, including derived types.
Primitive collection items must be compatible with the expected element type and nullability; scalar and collection expression shapes must agree.
A navigation binding path cannot occur twice on the same source; distinct type-cast paths are permitted.
Bindings describe related entities from one set; when paths differ only by casts, the most specific path applies to the instance.
obligations.policy: Static validation preserves distinct typed paths and rejects duplicate paths. Choosing a binding for an actual entity and confirming its related entities belong to the target set are runtime consumer responsibilities.

obligations.requirement: Structural and navigation property names share a uniqueness scope within the declaring structured type.
A declared property cannot have the declaring type's name. Sharing a base or derived type's name is permitted.
An XML reference requires Uri and at least one Include or IncludeAnnotations child.
Include requires Namespace; JSON includes are objects in an array. Alias is optional.
IncludeAnnotations requires TermNamespace; JSON entries are objects in an array. Qualifier and TargetNamespace are optional.
An included namespace cannot recur even across separate reference documents.
Type names are unique in the schema namespace across type kinds.
Schema namespaces cannot be Edm, odata, System or Transient.
An optional schema alias is a simple identifier.
XML Schema requires Namespace and permits Alias.
An XML annotation group requires Target and permits Qualifier.
An XML annotation group contains at least one Annotation.
Every reference specifies a document-identifying URI.
Two references cannot specify the same URI.
Reference URLs should locate documents, or identify well-known schemas.
Relative reference URIs use document identity and applicable XML Base.
An enumeration member name is a simple identifier.
Member names are unique within the enumeration type.
Member names are case-sensitive; authors should avoid case-only distinctions.
obligations.policy: Accept case-distinct names; optional author lint, as described in advisory-policies.json.

obligations.requirement: IEEE754Compatible=true emits Int64 and Decimal numbers as strings.
IEEE754Compatible=false or absent emits numbers as JSON numbers.
Instance paths have at most one unselected collection segment; key predicates and ordered indexes select individual items.
Remaining single-valued segments are evaluated for each instance in the unselected collection.
obligations.policy: The resolver preserves collection multiplicity and typed item-relative segments. Evaluating values for actual instances belongs to an expression evaluator.

obligations.requirement: An index segment is an integer literal after an ordered collection-valued structural property.
Indexes are zero-based; negative indexes count from the end; remaining segments evaluate relative to the selected item.
obligations.policy: Resolver retains a typed index and item-relative endpoint. Selecting runtime values is the expression evaluator's responsibility.

obligations.requirement: Authors should consider client precision limits and clients must account for round-trip data loss.
obligations.policy: Preserve decimal text in metadata; application value editing and PATCH policy belong to the client.
